linux_findings: File dialog: makepad's Linux file dialog is neither xdg-desktop-portal nor GTK. It runs the desktop's own helper, the first of zenity, qarma, matedialog and kdialog on PATH (kdialog first under KDE), and reads the chosen path from its output (.sources/makepad/platform/src/os/linux/file_dialog.rs). The build host has none of them, so file_dialogs::native_file_bytes_supported() is false: files.status answers import_supported false, and the shell does not offer files.import at all. PDF Tools then shows 'Not available here' beside 'Open a PDF from this device', and the button shows the banner 'This OctoSense can't open files from the device for PDF Tools.' Nothing hangs, and nothing is logged as an error. On Linux, ui.py now checks that (open_on_linux).

On Linux the shell's window is mapped on the run's own weston (MAKEPAD_HIDE_WINDOWS does nothing there). The files service counts a window outside macOS as focused until it reports losing focus (crates/shell/src/files_service/mod.rs, Foreground). So with a helper on PATH the dialog really opens. That is why ui.py leaves the step out when a helper is on PATH, and why the stand-in helper's check could run a real import.

A real import, which no test had run before (on the Mac the hidden window has the dialog refused): the helper was asked 'zenity --file-selection --title=Import a file into this app'. The chosen 'Lease 2026.pdf' (16,477 bytes) was copied byte for byte into accounts/device/library/Imported PDF.pdf. library.json titled it 'Lease 2026', 7 pages, with its cover. It opened in a tab, 'Lease 2026.pdf', on '1 / 7'. The import passes no file filter (the files service adds one only for photos), so the dialog would list every file, on every platform.

Fonts and text: the host has only DejaVu (8 font files in fontconfig), and nothing differs from macOS. The shell's interface draws with Makepad's bundled fonts, and the engine's page renders (the samples' sans-serif and serif text) match the Mac's. compare/ shows Home, a page, find and an edited paragraph beside the macOS frames of the same steps: the same text, wrapping and layout, and the same storage numbers. CJK text was not exercised.

Software GL: each shell's start stalls its UI thread: a 3.1 to 3.6 s first event, then draw-list stalls of 0.5 to 1.2 s whose sampled frames are LLVM compiling (Mesa's llvmpipe builds its shaders; one more such compile, of 0.55 to 0.65 s, comes with the first page). Apart from those, no UI-thread stall logged in the five runs was longer than 409 ms, and no script handler overran 64 ms in any of them.

Window size: on weston the shell's window is 1400 x 900 points at dpi 1. The log says 'wm: pdftools asks for a 1536x1024 window; it opens at 1296x698 (the dock covers 78 points of the desk)', an app area of 1292 x 662, the wide layout: the same as the macOS hidden shell (1400 x 898). Opened from the menu once the desk had drawn, it is 1296 x 709 (app area 1292 x 673), ending above the dock; the macOS hidden shell's 1400 x 897 window gave 1296 x 703. Both sizes were the same on main 3a563057, which has #485 (the dock hides only while OctoSense is full screen or, on Wayland, maximized; the shell's window on weston is neither) and #487.

Read mode: in both runs, light and dark, it was entered from the floating bar on 2 / 4. Tabs, mode bar, rail, panels and status line were gone. A page turned to 3 / 4 and the zoom went from 100% to 125%. It was left by Exit read mode (light) or the corner control (dark), on 3 / 4 at 125%.

Comment dates: in the host's own zone, UTC, the highlight read 'Today 14:25' at 14:25 UTC. Local time is UTC there, so that alone cannot tell the two apart. With TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati (UTC+14, already 12 Oct) it read 'Today 04:32' at 14:32 UTC on 11 Oct. The pdf service's conversion and the app's std.local_time both take the offset from localtime_r's tm_gmtoff (crates/shell/src/shell/bar.rs sets the script's offset), and they agree across the date change.

ext4: every home was on ext4. pdf.save's staging and rename, the render cache's writes and the covers all passed at 64 ms with no overrun, at load averages of 10 to 35, in five runs. On the Mac the 64 ms runs overran after 262 and 555 ms renames, at load averages of 54 to 74; the loads differ, so this is not a like-for-like timing comparison. After the restart the five current covers were kept with the same nanosecond modification times, and only the new import's cover was drawn. Remove deleted the PDF's cover. The cache evicts by modification time (cache.rs), not by directory order, which differs between ext4 and APFS.

The same numbers as on the Mac: the storage line read '187 KB of 64 MB used' for 191,793 bytes, and the samples' covers had the same name hashes and sizes. Only the combined PDF differs, by one byte (10,535 here, 10,534 there).
